# Code of conduct

This project is run by one person as a personal toolkit, shared publicly under MIT. The bar for participation here is low (be a reasonable adult), but it's worth being explicit about what that means so there's something to point to if it stops being true.

## Where this applies

Anywhere related to this project: issues, pull requests, code comments, and any direct communication about the work.

## What's expected

- Stay focused on the technical work.
- Argue about decisions and code. Stay off the people behind them.
- Assume the other party is acting in good faith until there's evidence otherwise.
- If you make a mistake, fix it. A short apology is enough.

## What's not acceptable

- Personal attacks, harassment, or hostility.
- Discriminatory language or behaviour, including on the basis of race, gender, sexuality, religion, age, ability, or appearance.
- Trolling, brigading, or deliberately wasting other people's time.
- Publishing someone's private information without their permission.
- Sexualised language or imagery in any context related to this project.

If a reasonable person would think something else is out of bounds, treat it as out of bounds too.

## Reporting

If someone's behaviour towards you on this project crosses a line, email ben.jackson@infosek.com.au. Reports are confidential.

This is a one-maintainer project. If the issue is with the maintainer, you have a few options: raise it in the relevant issue or PR, escalate to [GitHub Support](https://support.github.com/), or step away. Honesty about the limitation is more useful than a fictional appeals process.

## What happens after a report

I'll acknowledge the report within a reasonable timeframe and look into it. Depending on what I find, responses might include:

- A private conversation with the person whose behaviour was reported.
- A public note in the relevant issue or PR.
- Locking or hiding specific comments.
- Blocking the person from the repository, temporarily or permanently.

I'll communicate the outcome to the person who reported the issue.

## Scope and inspiration

The structure of this document draws on the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/) and similar open-source codes of conduct. It's deliberately shorter and more direct than the Contributor Covenant itself, which is written for larger communities than this one.
